title: How to find and win your first 10 B2B customers: a seven-step sequence from trust outward
summary: Part four of Lenny's B2B series distills how dozens of top startups (Figma, Gong, Retool, Vanta, Canva, Ramp) landed their first 10 customers. The core pattern is concentric circles of trust: start with your network, then creative cold outbound, investor networks, communities, content, press, and launch. None of it scales, which is why it works.

principles.text: Early-customer tactics don't scale, and that is why they work. B2B starts with hand-to-hand combat.
principles.quote: None of these seven strategies scale. That’s why they work. In B2B, it always starts with hand-to-hand combat.

principles.text: Start with your own network and your early employees' networks; they carry the most innate trust and least skepticism.
principles.quote: This group will have the most innate trust (and the lowest amount of skepticism) about your idea.

principles.text: Cold outbound works early if you are creative and targeted; if responses are poor, get more specific.
principles.quote: One of the recurring themes (and biggest surprises) across my interviews is the value, and effectiveness, of going cold outbound in the early stages

principles.text: Use investors' networks by digging in and cold-emailing yourself, not just asking for intros, and ask those founders for further intros.
principles.quote: But not by asking for introductions—instead, by doing the hard work of digging into the investors’ own networks (including batch-mates within YC) and cold-emailing them.

principles.text: In communities, add value first; nobody wants to pay attention to someone who only shows up to pitch.
principles.quote: When joining communities, focus first on adding value to the community. No one wants to pay attention to you if you’re there just to pitch your product.

principles.text: Trust is the secret weapon: start with the highest-trust channels and work outward.
principles.quote: Start with the channels that have the most innate levels of trust, and work your way outward.
